item.title: Jensen Huang and NVIDIA Facing Federal Investigations
item.description:
Jensen Huang is out as Nvidia's CEO, but for the founder and longtime face of both the company and the AI race, the chips are still hitting the fan. Federal investigators and lawmakers on Capitol Hill are seeking answers on any potential wrongdoing, investigations as the fallout from Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy grows wider. Attorney General Todd Blanche says “of course” the FBI is investigating whether Alice Huang is a spy, adding "the DOJ has a role in investigating if there are chips that shouldn't be sold.” Sources tell FOX Business Huang has agreed to testify under oath on his business dealings with China as lawmakers probe the national security implications of his actions.
FOX's Tonya J. Powers speaks with Darren Botelho, Washington D.C. based correspondent for the FOX Business Network, who shares the latest in this rapidly changing story.

item.title: Gov. Ron DeSantis On What’s Next—For Him And The GOP
item.description:
The sudden resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang amid allegations of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy is colliding with urgent national security concerns in Washington over how America protects its advanced AI technology. Fox News Sunday Anchor and Host of the Livin’ the Bream Podcast Shannon Bream joins to discuss the looming congressional subpoenas and federal investigations into potential export control violations, what Huang’s departure without a formal succession plan means for the U.S.–China AI race, and the bipartisan pressure on the White House to tighten tech regulations
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis joins FOX News Senior White House Correspondent Peter Doocy for a post-midterm breakdown as he prepares to leave office in January. DeSantis explains why he believes Republicans fell short in key races, arguing the party lost focus on the economy, inflation and affordability while overlooking the issues voters care about most. Plus, he weighs in on the GOP’s path forward, what President Trump can do to regain momentum, and what’s next for his own political future.
Plus, commentary by Paul Mauro, FOX News contributor, providing legal, political, and criminal justice analysis across FOX News Media platforms.

item.title: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang Resigns Amid Multiple Affairs
item.description:
Nvidia shares falling 8% just hours before CEO Jensen Huang announced his resignation. In addition to cheating on his wife with Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese spy and executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, it was revealed the chipmaker chief was also unfaithful with Kimberly Powell, a senior executive at Nvidia who reports to him. The fallout from the affairs and Huang’s potential ouster extends well beyond a single sector.
FOX's Gurnal Scott speaks with Gary Kaltbaum, President Of Kaltbaum Capital Management, FOX Business Network contributor, and host of the radio show “Investors Edge”, who says NVIDIA needs to push through this rough patch quickly and show investors they are still leaders in the tech world.

item.title: Democrats Go on the Attack: Are Republicans Ready?
item.description:
As Republicans head into the minority on Capitol Hill, House Republicans have selected Ohio Congressman Jim Jordan as their minority leader while Senate Republicans stick with John Thune. Former White House Chief of Staff and FOX News political analyst Reince Priebus joins White House correspondent Aishah Hasnie to examine how this new congressional leadership team will navigate the final two years of the Trump administration. Priebus discusses why Jordan’s reputation as a fighter gives him unique leverage to cut deals, how the White House is preparing for an onslaught of Democratic subpoenas, and why President Trump’s next press secretary will require a litigation mindset to handle the coming political warfare.
As concerns grow over “forever chemicals” in everyday consumer products, new research is raising questions about the link between PFAS exposure and breast cancer. National Cancer Institute Director Dr. Anthony Letai unpacks a new study linking these chemicals to a stubborn form of breast cancer, explains why a dramatic drop in public exposure should reassure people, and outlines the proven lifestyle factors that truly protect long-term health.
PLUS, commentary by Jason Rantz, author of What’s Killing America, and the host of The Jason Rantz Show.

item.title: 'Make Camo Your Cause' Dedicated to Ending Veteran Homelessness
item.description:
The Department of Veterans Affairs found that in January 2025, more than 32-thousand veterans were experiencing homelessness. This veterans day, we’re turning the tables and taking a look at how the country can support them. Fox Corporation is partnering with U.S.VETS for the "Make Camo Your Cause" campaign for the sixth straight year and encourages all Americans to use the #HONORUSVETS hashtag to help raise awareness.
FOX's Tonya J. Powers speaks with Larry D. Williams, the Vice President of Programs at U.S.VETS, where he leads the national "Make Camo Your Cause" campaign, who shares how his organization focuses on veteran support, family reunification, housing stability, and mental health programs.
Go here to learn more and donate: usvets.org or honor.usvets.org/givetoday

item.title: Are Changes Coming to ICE?
item.description:
Despite Republican midterm setbacks and demographic shifts among suburban and Hispanic voters, President Trump has doubled down on hardline immigration enforcement. Former Acting ICE Director Todd Lyons speaks with FOX News congressional correspondent Bill Melugin to analyze the political fallout and ICE’s operational pivot toward discreet interior enforcement. Lyons also discusses whether immigration policies cost Republicans at the ballot box, and outlines his opposition to mass amnesty for immigration offenses.
This Veterans Day, political battles in Washington over Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s military decisions are colliding with urgent questions about how America truly supports its troops. Marine veteran and Medal of Honor recipient Dakota Meyer defends Hegseth against congressional attacks, outlines his new mission leading a military task force to overhaul squalid living conditions in troop barracks, and explains why prioritizing the needs of service members is essential to restoring trust and military readiness.
PLUS, commentary by Jason Chaffetz, FOX News contributor and the host of the Jason In The House podcast on FOX News Radio.
